frontmatter.title: Use Coercion for Form and Query Data
frontmatter.impactDescription: Form data and query params are always strings; without coercion, z.number() rejects "42" and z.boolean() rejects "true

frontmatter.title: Handle All Validation Issues Not Just First
frontmatter.impactDescription: Showing only the first error forces users to fix-submit-fix repeatedly; collecting all errors improves UX dramatically

frontmatter.title: Validate at System Boundaries
frontmatter.impactDescription: Validating deep in business logic allows corrupt data to propagate; validating at boundaries catches issues before they spread

frontmatter.title: Use z.unknown() Instead of z.any()
frontmatter.impactDescription: z.any() bypasses TypeScript's type system entirely; z.unknown() forces type narrowing before use

frontmatter.title: Rule Title Here

frontmatter.title: Export Both Schemas and Inferred Types
frontmatter.impactDescription: Exporting only schemas forces consumers to derive types themselves; exporting both reduces boilerplate and improves DX

frontmatter.title: Avoid Double Validation
frontmatter.impactDescription: Parsing the same data twice wastes CPU cycles; in hot paths this adds measurable latency

frontmatter.title: Return False Instead of Throwing in Refine
frontmatter.impactDescription: Throwing in refine stops validation early, hiding other errors; returning false allows Zod to collect all issues

frontmatter.title: Use Discriminated Unions for Type Narrowing
frontmatter.impactDescription: Regular unions require manual type guards; discriminated unions enable TypeScript's automatic narrowing and Zod's optimized parsing
